ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all partners, general partners, directors, and authorized agents under PCMLTFA s. 9 (foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs, and heads of international organizations) in accordance with the FINTRAC Politically Exposed Persons and Heads of International Organizations Guideline (2024 edition, as amended). Screening must cover the United Nations Consolidated List, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, Canada's autonomous sanctions schedules enacted under SEMA (including the Special Economic Measures (Russia) Regulations and Special Economic Measures (Iran) Regulations), and Interpol Red Notices where available. Screening results must be documented in the LP's AML/CFT risk assessment and refreshed at least every 90 days for the operational life of the LP.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (RegCorps), administered by Service Alberta and the Corporate Registry Branch; official informational portal: https://www.alberta.ca/corporate-registry; NUANS name search is procured through authorized Alberta registry service providers.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Alberta Business Names Regulation and the Registrar's Name Decision Guidelines, an LP name must contain three elements: (1) a distinctive element (e.g., OCEAN CAR CARRIER), (2) a descriptive element (e.g., SHIPPING, TRANSPORT, or LOGISTICS), and (3) a legal element (Limited Partnership, L.P., or LP). Names must be expressed in English or French using the Latin alphabet; non-Latin-script trade names must be transliterated into Latin characters and submitted for NUANS searchability. Numerals, brackets, hyphens, ampersands, and lexical spelling variants may be used provided the name remains distinctive and not misleading.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Where the Registrar declines the NUANS name (due to a conflicting existing registration, misleading connotation, or the use of a restricted token without ministerial consent), the applicant or its authorized registry service provider may file a written Request for Reconsideration / Name Decision Review with the Alberta Corporate Registry within 30 days of the refusal letter. The request must attach the official refusal notice, the NUANS search report, evidence of prior use or registered rights in the relevant business class, any letters of no objection, and a corrected name in the alternative. If the Registrar confirms the refusal, further appeal lies by way of originating application to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta within 30 days under the Alberta Partnerships Act, RSA 2000, c. P-7, s. 20, read with the Alberta Rules of Court. An approved name reservation is valid for 90 days with a single 90-day extension available on written request before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A commercial virtual office (an Alberta physical street address, mail-forwarding service, and records-hosting arrangement) is permissible provided that the registered office is not a private mailbox and that the LP can always be physically located at that address for service of process, audit, inspection, and FINTRAC examination. A post office box address alone is statutorily impermissible.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 3% to 5% annual probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by Alberta registry compliance officers or FINTRAC examiners for a Low_Risk_Standard entity; probability rises to approximately 15% or more where the LP maintains a virtual-only address without accessible books and records.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — My Business Account portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html); Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration (TRA) for Alberta provincial tax administration (https://www.alberta.ca/taxes). Alberta does not levy a provincial sales tax; GST/HST is administered exclusively by the CRA under the Excise Tax Act (Canada).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For an Alberta limited partnership (LP) engaged in deep-sea Ro-Ro vehicle transport, the LP must first register under the Partnership Act (Alberta) as an extra-provincial or domestic limited partnership. The statutory tax identifier is the CRA Business Number (BN), which is obtained by filing Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) or, for non-resident applicants, the corresponding CRA non-resident registration procedure. The BN is a nine-digit number with program-specific accounts; the GST/HST account is identified by the two-letter program code 'RT'. The application must state the partnership's legal name, Alberta registration number, principal place of business, all Canadian and non-resident limited and general partners' names and addresses, the nature of the commercial activity (ISIC 5012 / NAICS 483111), and a Canadian representative/attorney for service if the partnership has no permanent establishment in Canada. The GST/HST registration threshold is C$30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; because an ocean carrier's freight revenues will normally exceed that threshold, GST/HST registration is mandatory once supplies are made in Canada. Foreign partners that do not themselves carry on business in Canada do not require a separate BN; they are identified in the T5013 partnership information return and taxed under Part I or Part XIII of the Income Tax Act.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a U.S.-style check-the-box election. An Alberta LP is fiscally transparent for Canadian income tax under ITA s.96; income and loss are allocated to partners and taxed at the partner level. For GST/HST, however, the LP is treated as a separate person and may be required to register. Relevant statutory elections include: voluntary GST/HST registration under ETA s.240(1); election of a fiscal period under ITA s.249.1; a non-resident partner's election under ITA s.216 to compute tax on Canadian-source income; and treaty-based transparent-entity rules under the Canada-U.S. Tax Convention Article IV(6). For hybrid mismatch situations, a Canadian LP with U.S. partners may be characterized as a corporation under U.S. check-the-box, and anti-avoidance rules can apply where a payment gives rise to a deduction in one jurisdiction without corresponding inclusion in the other.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax — Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act (ETA). Alberta applies only the 5% federal GST; there is no Alberta provincial sales tax or HST component.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — the 'small supplier' threshold under ETA s.148(1), measured on worldwide taxable supplies of goods and services (including zero-rated supplies) in the immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters. A non-resident carrier making taxable supplies in Canada in the course of a commercial activity, or whose worldwide taxable revenues exceed the threshold, must register and collect GST/HST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not impose a mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoicing, or digital stamping regime. The CRA does not require pre-clearance of taxable sales; electronic invoices are accepted, and GST/HST returns must be filed electronically through GST/HST NETFILE or a CRA-approved service provider. Record-keeping obligations under ETA s.286 require all invoices, contracts, bills of lading, customs entries, and payment records to be retained for six years in an accessible electronic or paper format. The Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing Interoperability Framework is voluntary; Peppol-based e-invoicing may be used but is not mandated at the federal or Alberta level.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of a service of transporting motor vehicles by ship from a place in Canada to a place outside Canada by a Ro-Ro deep-sea carrier is zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V of the Excise Tax Act (freight transportation services), provided the supplier retains documentary evidence that the goods were physically exported from Canada and delivered to a foreign destination. The zero rate applies to the ocean carriage leg of an export movement, whether procured by a Canadian exporter, a non-resident buyer, or a charterer. Domestic feeder transportation within Canada may be taxable unless separately supplied as part of a single export service. The carrier is entitled to claim near-full input tax credits for goods and services acquired in Canada to perform zero-rated export transportation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration filed through the Canadian Automated Export Declarations System (CAED) or Form B13A export reporting, where required under the Customs Act
Original or electronic ocean Bill of Lading (Ro-Ro vessel) showing Canadian load port, foreign discharge port, cargo description, consignee, and destination outside Canada
Commercial invoice and packing list for the vehicles being exported
Booking confirmation, voyage charter party, or service contract evidencing the ocean transportation arrangement and foreign destination
Inward remittance certificate or SWIFT/Wire transfer record (e.g., MT103) proving receipt of freight payment in foreign currency or Canadian dollars from the counterparty
Proof of foreign customs import or port clearance at the destination country where available
Export permits or vehicle registration documents where the exported goods are subject to export control
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess zero-rated export claims within the normal four-year limitation period (unlimited in cases of misrepresentation, neglect, or wilful default). If a carrier fails to substantiate physical exportation, foreign destination, or payment repatriation within the contractual/statutory period, the supply is re-rated at 5% GST, related input tax credits are disallowed, interest is charged on the net tax from the date the return was filed or due, and civil penalties may apply under ETA s.280 (general compliance penalty) and s.285 (gross negligence equal to the greater of C$100 and 50% of the understated net tax). False statements and fraudulent zero-rating claims can also trigger injunctions and criminal prosecution under ETA s.327, with fines up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment. CRA export audits require full traceability from booked cargo to foreign customs clearance and foreign-currency receipt.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates a free current account convertibility regime with no prior approval required for trade settlements, profit remittances, or operational FX transactions. Capital account transactions remain subject to Bank of Canada reporting obligations and Investment Canada Act restrictions. Profit distributions to limited partners are freely remittable without surrender mandates, provided full FINTRAC compliance and tax documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion of export proceeds required under Canadian foreign exchange law. Canadian banks process repatriation of ocean carrier receipts through standard correspondent channels. Exporters must file FINTRAC foreign exchange transaction reports within prescribed timelines; no conversion ratio or surrender percentage applies.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability for offshore digital EMIs. Canadian limited partnerships face heightened FINTRAC scrutiny on cross-border digital payment rails; traditional correspondent banking remains the compliant channel.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors, authorized signatories, and controlling partners must attend in-person KYC interviews and account opening at Canadian commercial banks. Remote electronic onboarding is not permitted for limited partnerships with international trade exposure or high-value transaction volumes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Limited Partnership, partnership agreement, director resolutions, proof of address, beneficial ownership declarations, and tax filings

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shipping industry sanctions and trade license screening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Vessel registration certificates, Canadian Transport Authority licenses, insurance documentation, and confirmation of compliance with Canadian sanctions lists

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital via domestic wire transfers (SWIFT MT103) using purpose code 998 or 999 for partner contributions. Verification requires partnership agreement amendments, capital contribution resolutions, and supporting tax documentation. All transactions subject to FINTRAC reporting thresholds and beneficial ownership disclosure.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for RORO shipping settlements via SWIFT MT103 with purpose codes 1000 (trade payment) or issuance of commercial letters of credit through correspondent banks. All disbursements require supporting shipping documents, bills of lading, and invoice verification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each anniversary of the LP's registration date under the Partnership Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c P-3
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attaches Service Alberta late-filing charges and flags the LP as non-compliant; if the return remains unfiled for more than 12 months after the anniversary, the Registrar may issue notice and, after a 60-day cure period, cancel/strike off the LP's registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Corporate Registry Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed with the annual return within 30 days after each registration anniversary; interim changes to beneficial ownership must be reported within 15 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence-level penalties up to CAD 100,000–500,000 per default plus personal liability for the general partner; materially inaccurate or omitted UBO confirmation may also support cancellation of the LP registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Calgary Tax Centre
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the LP's fiscal year-end (for a December 31 year-end: on or before May 31 of the following year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CRA penalty of CAD 30 per day (maximum CAD 2,500 per return) for late T5013 filing, plus CAD 25 per day per omitted partner T5013 slip (maximum CAD 2,500 per slip); gross-negligence penalties under Section 163 of the Income Tax Act may also apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Reconciliation and Filing (where applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The annual GST/HST return must be filed within 3 months after the fiscal year-end (for a December 31 year-end: on or before March 31 of the following year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CRA penalty of 1% of unpaid tax plus 0.25% per month up to 12 months, or a 5% late-filing penalty plus 5% per month where a return is demanded; interest is compounded daily on outstanding amounts.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No blanket statutory audit is imposed on a private Alberta LP under the Partnership Act. A mandatory independent audit is triggered only where (i) the LP is a reporting issuer under Canadian securities legislation, (ii) the limited partnership agreement or a lender/government covenant requires audited financial statements, or (iii) the LP conducts a federally or provincially regulated financial activity. As a low-risk commercial Ro-Ro shipping partnership, no statutory audit is required at formation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian ASPE (Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook) is the default framework for a private LP; IFRS applies if the LP becomes publicly accountable, is a reporting issuer, or if the partnership agreement or lending institutions mandate IFRS financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The general partner must maintain a current register of beneficial owners identifying every individual with direct or indirect ownership of 25% or more of the partnership interests. UBO particulars must be reconfirmed with the Alberta Corporate Registry via the annual return within 30 days of each registration anniversary, and any material change must be reported within 15 days. The register must be kept at the Alberta registered office and is subject to inspection by registry authorities.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (Limited and General Partners)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300–800 per annum (CAD 400–1,100) for a Calgary- or Edmonton-based corporate services provider covering the registered office, partnership administration, and annual-return filing
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000–35,000 (CAD 16,000–48,000) for a full certified audit of an LP operating a Ro-Ro vessel; a review engagement typically costs USD 4,000–12,000 where no audit is statutorily required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23.0% combined headline rate (federal general corporate rate of 15.0% plus Alberta provincial general corporate rate of 8.0%); the Alberta limited partnership is a flow-through vehicle and is not itself assessed at this rate, but its corporate partners are taxable at the combined rate on their allocable share of Canadian-source business income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No Alberta statutory tax holiday for ISIC 5012 deep-sea Ro-Ro operators; incentive levers include accelerated capital cost allowance on vessels (Class 7 at 15% declining balance and Class 41 at 8% declining balance), the federal and Alberta small business deduction for qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporate partners only (9% federal + 2% Alberta on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income), and treaty Article 8 exemption or reduction for non-resident partners' international-shipping income where a permanent establishment is not established in Canada.
